name: Placki Ziemniaczane (Potato Pancakes)
summary: Grated potato and onion fried into crisp pancakes, served with sour cream.
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion on the fine side of a box grater into a large bowl.
Tip into a sieve set over a bowl and press out as much liquid as you can. Let the liquid sit 2 minutes, pour off the water, and keep the white potato starch at the bottom.
Mix the grated potato, the starch, eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Drop in heaped spoonfuls, flatten to about 1 cm, and fry 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Add oil between batches.
Drain on paper towel and keep warm in a low oven while you fry the rest. Serve hot with sour cream.

substitutions.substitute: 3 tbsp cornstarch, or simply more of the saved potato starch

glutenFree.notes: Potatoes, onion, eggs, and sour cream are naturally gluten-free. The small amount of flour is the only source of gluten.

budgetNotes: Squeezing out the liquid is what makes them crisp. Wet batter makes soggy pancakes.
In Poland they're eaten with sour cream for a savoury meal, or with sugar or applesauce as a sweet one. Both are traditional.
